items.entity: Downward 2x2-element load patch on right edge (loading condition of Fig. 7(a))
items.description: The Fig. 7 caption (Sec. 3.3) says only that (a) vf=0.3 and (b) vf=0.5 share 'the same loading condition'. The load index is never given. Sec. 4.1 defines 18 positions of a 2x2 patch that steps down the right edge 2 rows at a time (index 1 = top), and Fig. 9 shows index 8. In Table 1, positions 1/9/17 appear at vf 0.3 and 4/9/13 at vf 0.5, so index 9 is the only shared one. The actual position is shown only in the figure.
readings: Index 9: element rows 17-18 from top, patch spans 0.444-0.500 of edge height from top (centre ~0.472H); matches Table 1 case vf 0.3 / pos 9, C = 1.989e-3 J
Index 8 (as drawn in Fig. 9): rows 15-16, spans 0.389-0.444H from top (centre ~0.417H)
Index 10: rows 19-20, spans 0.500-0.556H from top (just below mid-height)
Index 1: top-right corner, 0-0.056H from top
Index 17: rows 33-34, spans 0.889-0.944H from top
Any other index k=1..18: rows 2k-1..2k, spanning (2k-2)/36 to 2k/36 of H from top

items.entity: Design domain shape and discretisation for Fig. 7
items.description: Sec. 3.3 / Fig. 7 gives no domain or mesh information. The cantilever setup (square domain, 36x36 elements, aluminium, 2x2 load patch) appears only later in Sec. 4.1 and has to be assumed to apply. The paper also mentions other sizes (64x64 in the abstract and Sec. 4.2, '60x60' in Sec. 5).
readings: Square domain, 36 x 36 square elements (Sec. 4.1 setup)
Square domain at another resolution (e.g. 64 x 64) with the same 4-pixel filter radius, if Fig. 7 was generated separately

items.entity: Uniformly distributed load over 2x2 elements next to right edge
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says a 'vertically downward uniformly distributed force is applied on a small area occupying 2x2 elements next to the right edge'; Sec. 2.1 says it is a 'distributed load' whose location varies 'along the right edge'. The text does not say whether this is a body/area load on the four elements (the per-pixel CNN force channel suggests so) or an edge traction, or how it becomes nodal forces.
readings: Uniform body force on the 2x2 elements in the two rightmost columns -> consistent nodal loads on the 3x3 patch nodes, weights 1:2:1 / 2:4:2 / 1:2:1 (/16)
Equal vertical forces on all 9 nodes of the 2x2 patch
Uniform traction on the right-boundary segment of the patch (2 element edges, 3 nodes, weights 1:2:1)
Equal vertical forces on the 3 right-edge nodes of the patch

items.description: Sec. 2.1 says the load has 'a fixed magnitude', but no value (total force or intensity) is given anywhere. Compliances are reported in 1e-3 J.
readings: Total force 1 N
Total force 1 kN
Unit force per loaded element (total 4 units)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only a 'square design domain' of 36x36 elements. Physical dimensions and thickness are never given, even though E0 is in GPa and compliance in J.

items.entity: 2D elasticity assumption (plane stress vs plane strain)
items.description: Only 'two-dimensional linear problems' is stated (Sec. 5). With nu0=0.3 (Sec. 4.1), plane strain gives an effective Poisson ratio of about 0.43 instead of 0.3.
readings: Plane stress
Plane strain

items.description: Eq. (1) gives void regions only 'a small value' to avoid a singular stiffness matrix; no number is given.
readings: Emin = 1e-9 * E0
Emin = 1e-6 * E0
Emin = 1e-3 * E0

items.description: Sec. 2 says only 'p is the penalization parameter, usually p = 3'. It does not confirm p for this example or say whether p is ramped up during the run.
readings: p = 3 constant
p ramped from 1 to 3

items.entity: Density projection use and filter/projection chain
items.description: Sec. 2 says the Wang et al. (2011) projection 'can be used' (beta0=1, eta=0.5), next to a sensitivity filter of radius 4 px. It is unclear: (1) whether projection was applied in the FEM-SIMP benchmark runs behind Fig. 7; (2) which field is projected, since no density filter is mentioned and Wang et al. projection normally acts on a density-filtered field; (3) whether vf=0.3 is measured on projected or raw densities.
readings: Sensitivity filter r=4 only, no projection
Sensitivity filter r=4 + tanh projection (eta=0.5) applied directly to design variables; volume on projected densities
Density filter r=4 + tanh projection (standard Wang et al. chain); volume on projected densities
Sensitivity filter + projection; volume constraint on unprojected design variables

items.description: Sec. 2 says beta 'is initially set as 1 and enlarges gradually'. The increase rule, how often it increases and the final beta are not given.
readings: Double beta every 50 iterations (1->2->4->8) over ~150 iterations
Double beta every 25 iterations up to beta = 32
Increase beta by 1 every 10 iterations up to beta ~ 16

items.description: Eq. (4) is an equality volume constraint. Eqs. (5)-(6) turn it into an unconstrained objective in which a 'Lagrange multiplier' lambda multiplies the squared volume violation (a penalty form; note the factor 2 in Eq. 6). The value and update rule of lambda are not given, so how exactly vf=0.3 is reached is undetermined.
readings: Fixed penalty weight lambda (user-chosen constant); final volume only approximately 0.3
lambda increased/updated each iteration (augmented-Lagrangian style) until |V-0.3| < tolerance
Exact enforcement of V=0.3 via OC bisection or MMA instead

items.description: Sec. 2 says densities are updated with 'the gradient descent method' using filtered sensitivities. Step size, sensitivity scaling, move limit and how the bounds 0<=rho<=1 are enforced are not given.
readings: Fixed step size on normalised sensitivities, move limit 0.2, clip to [0,1]
Step size chosen by line search, clip to [0,1]
Use the standard OC update instead (move 0.2, damping exponent 0.5)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only that 'the average number of iterations in each design is 150'. No stopping rule is given.
readings: Fixed 150 iterations
Stop when max density change < 0.01
Stop when beta reaches its maximum and max density change < 0.01

items.description: No passive (fixed solid or void) regions are mentioned. Sec. 4.1 notes that some NN-accelerated designs have no material where the load is applied, which implies the load patch can be designed. This is never stated for the FEM benchmark behind Fig. 7.
